newsitem.title: USA: Alcoa up after oversold condition - analyst.
newsitem.headline: Alcoa up after oversold condition - analyst.

text.p: -- Alcoa shares were up Thursday on the New York Stock Exchange because they were likely oversold following the company's release of third-quarter results last Friday, said Tom VanLeeuwen, metals analyst at CS First Boston.
-- Shares were up 2-1/8 in morning trading. A company spokeswoman said Alcoa "has not put out any news releases."
-- "We think we're just recapturing some of the volatility in our stock, after we announced earnings," she said.
-- Alcoa last Friday posted third-quarter earnings of $0.77 per share on an operating basis, below Wall Street's consensus estimate of $0.95 per share.
-- Shares tumbled 2-1/4 Friday following the earnings announcement.
-- "I guess this is proof that dead cats bounce," VanLeeuwen said. "The stock was probably oversold and there's nothing really of a fundamental nature to cause this."
